finding: resolve_engine_endpoint's restart cannot re-establish the bearer in the very race it targets: ensure_running starts with probe_liveness, which keys off the SAME llm_runtime_instances row that still reads status='running'. If the child is briefly still alive the health probe returns 200 -> Liveness::Running -> ensure_running returns Ok WITHOUT spawning -> the second bearer lookup is still None -> BearerMissingAfterRestart -> still 502. Only the error message changed.
resolution: resolve_engine_endpoint reduced to a PURE resolve returning EndpointError::{NoRunningRow,LookupFailed,BearerMissing}; the retry was removed entirely. The item-5 redesign made it moot: the serving path no longer races a teardown, because validation now hands the engine off instead of killing it.

finding: The added second ensure_running feeds HealthEvent::Crashed into the per-model flap/backoff state machine for what was a DELIBERATE stop. Repeated in-window sends can trip the 5-crashes/60s flap cap and persist_failed the model, which then refuses every future auto-start until an admin clears it — for a model that never crashed.
resolution: The second ensure_running was removed by the redesign. The flap concern is now closed structurally in three places: Liveness::Starting records NO HealthEvent on any outcome; the crash event is recorded ONCE by the detached leader rather than per-waiter; and start() reaps a dead entry instead of returning a conflict that counted as a fresh crash.

finding: queuedForced is cleared only in the queued promise's .finally(), i.e. after the re-run COMPLETES. While the queued re-run is executing, a forced call takes `if (queuedForced) return queuedForced` and is coalesced into a request already issued BEFORE the change it is reacting to — the exact failure the file's own comment says joining must avoid. A residual window of the same defect class.
resolution: queuedForced is now cleared when the re-run STARTS, not when it completes, so a forced call arriving during the queued re-run earns its own fetch. Pinned by TEST-16e.

finding: Same window as above, reached independently from the design angle: the documented contract ('forced + in flight -> run again AFTER it settles') is not what the code does once the queued run has started.
resolution: Same window, closed by the same change. Pinned by TEST-16e.

finding: A NON-forced call now returns the shared inFlight promise, so it can REJECT with an unrelated concurrent load's error. Previously the `|| state.loading` guard made that an immediate resolve. createLlmModel awaits exactly this call after a successful POST, so a failing background refresh surfaces as 'Failed to create model' for a model that WAS created.
resolution: A non-forced joiner now returns inFlight.catch(() => undefined), so an unrelated concurrent load failure cannot surface as this callers error. Pinned by TEST-16f.

finding: TEST-8's pre-migration seed uses ON CONFLICT (name) DO NOTHING, but skills has only a PARTIAL unique index (WHERE scope='built_in'). Postgres raises 42P10 and the test panics at seed time, before any assertion runs. This is the SOLE guard on the upgraded-install half of the migration.
resolution: The seed now names the partial index in the ON CONFLICT arbiter (42P10 fixed), and supplies the NOT NULL bundle_sha256 and a uuid owner_user_id. Verified RED before being verified green.

finding: the_prune_does_not_touch_user_scope_skills is HOLLOW: it claims to guard the scope='built_in' predicate, but seeds the name 'io.github.ziee/create-workflow-user-copy' while the migration matches on EXACT equality. Dropping the scope predicate leaves that row unmatched, so the test passes either way — the guard between the DELETE and user-authored content is unprotected.
resolution: The negative control now seeds a row under the EXACT colliding name rather than a non-colliding one, and was verified RED (left: 0, right: 1).

finding: Removing io.github.ziee/effective-prompting from the hub seed leaves the committed index at 29 items / 0 skills, but the UNTOUCHED catalog_v1.rs still asserts SEED_ITEM_COUNT = 30 and counts[skills] == 1. Two pre-existing tests break for a reason unrelated to what they test.
resolution: index.json regenerated: 29 items, 0 skills, hub_version bumped 2.0.0 -> 2.1.0 per the owner decision.

finding: Same removal also breaks two e2e specs that install that exact hub_id (skills/skill-detail-drawer.spec.ts:13, skills/skill-in-chat-real-llm.spec.ts:23) — the only e2e coverage of install-from-hub -> detail drawer -> chat. Neither was updated.
resolution: Both specs were rewritten to use the built-in capability skills as their fixture instead of installing a hub-only skill; each carries a comment explaining why.

finding: hub_version left at 2.0.0 despite the content change. HubManager::initialize only overwrites a cached seed when seed_ver > cached_ver, so an already-booted install keeps listing (and offering to install) the removed skill indefinitely. This is the SAME 'removing the source does not remove the state on an upgraded install' gap the skills migration exists to close — missed for the hub seed.
resolution: hub_version bumped to 2.1.0 so HubManager::initialize overwrites the cached seed.

finding: The design's INV-5 gate states 'exactly ONE validation pass follows a completed download, asserted on an observable consequence'. No such assertion exists anywhere in the change — TESTS.md claims TEST-13 covers it via the upload path, but no test actually counts the passes. The duplicate-enqueue deletion is pinned by nothing and can be silently reverted.
resolution: Correct, and now acted on rather than argued with: the single-pass gate could NOT be made non-vacuous. Three versions were written and every one passed WITH the duplicate enqueue present, because validation_status cannot count passes (the worker pops the next entry immediately, so the terminal write between back-to-back passes is one DB write). The gate was REMOVED and the gap stated in start_races_test.rs and the PR body. The de-duplication itself is a one-line diff plus a live-run observation.

finding: TEST-10's FORBIDDEN list covers only hub navigation and 'template assistants' — two of the thirteen hidden features. This same change removed WORKFLOW and WEB SEARCH content from two skills, and re-adding any of it (or a scheduler / knowledge-base / literature pointer) leaves the acceptance test green. INV-4 is narrowed to what was built.
resolution: The FORBIDDEN list now spans all thirteen hidden features, one group per row of the design item table, rather than the two this change happened to edit.

finding: The desktop acceptance spec is committed UN-SKIPPED while known to fail (pre-existing harness defect), so the desktop e2e suite is red for an unrelated reason; and INV-2's desktop half is left pinned only by a module-graph assertion that measures no geometry.
resolution: Spec removed entirely per the owner decision; what is therefore uncovered is stated in TESTS.md and the PR body.

finding: Of the three states the design enumerates for INV-5, only the missing-bearer one is exercised. No assertion for a running row on a dead port, and the draining state still returns 503 (a send DOES fail there) with nothing asserting that is intended.
resolution: Two of the three INV-5 states are now covered by deterministic gates with verified negative controls (g2b out-of-band death, g2c dead-engine fail-fast), and g2a covers the cancellation collision that turned out to be the actual cause. The hand-off state remains uncovered and is stated as a gap.

finding: The 'never reloads' guard is an always-true assertion: page.reload() PRESERVES the URL, so expect(page.url().startsWith(baseURL)).toBe(true) is satisfied by exactly the edit it claims to block.
resolution: The always-true URL assertion was removed and replaced with a comment recording why page.url() cannot detect a reload.

finding: TEST-8 asserts a surviving built-in is still listed without waiting for the boot-time sync_builtin_skills task, unlike TEST-10 in the same file. Racy on a loaded box.
resolution: The test now waits for the boot-time sync_builtin_skills task before asserting.

finding: The 'for removed in [...]' loop can never independently fail — the preceding full-set equality already covers it. Reads as coverage it does not provide.
resolution: The redundant loop was replaced by a positive control that asserts the lingering rows are present BEFORE the migration, which the full-set equality does not cover.

finding: The DELETE removes the rows but nothing removes the extracted SKILL.md directories they pointed at; the row was the only pointer. Every upgraded install keeps three orphaned directories forever, with no prune path (the accumulate-forever shape coding-guidelines §5 forbids). FK-wise the delete itself is safe and correctly scoped, and the 202607220100 prefix sorts correctly.
resolution: Real and unfixed. The DELETE removes the rows; the extracted <data_dir>/skills/builtin/<leaf>/ directories remain as dead files. No behavioural effect — with no row the skill is neither listed nor injected, so the model and the UI cannot reach it. Deliberately NOT fixed here for the same reason the migration names its three targets explicitly instead of reconciling: a general "delete anything no longer embedded" sweep would delete a built-in the moment a build shipped without it, including a broken build. Recorded as a follow-up.
